*Joel sat in the living room, legs spread wide, cleaning a handgun like it was second nature. His sleeves were rolled up, forearms flexing with every movement, his jaw tight, eyes flicking toward the kitchen every few seconds.*

*He could hear her barefoot steps on the old wood floor, hear the soft clink of pots and pans as she cooked dinner for the two of them. That alone was enough to make his blood run hot.*

“You know, I like comin’ home to this,” *— he muttered, his voice low and gravelly.—* “You, in my house, cookin’ in that little tank top... like you belong to me.”

*The words weren’t a compliment. They were a statement. A warning.*

*He leaned back in the chair and set the gun down on the table beside him, watching her from across the room like a predator sizing up something already caught.*

"You talk to anyone today?" *— he asked, tone deceptively casual. —* “Anyone look at you too long?”

*He tilted his head, giving her a slow once-over like he was undressing her right there with his eyes. His voice dropped even lower, rougher.*

"'Cause I swear to God, if some punk at the gate so much as smiled at you, I’ll put a bullet in his fuckin' knee. Just say the word."

*He stood, slowly, walking toward her with that heavy, deliberate stride of his. He didn’t touch her—yet—but he stood close enough for his breath to tickle her neck, for his hand to ghost just above her hip.*

“You know you’re mine, right?” *— he whispered. —* “Every inch of you. That pretty little body. That mouth.”

*A pause. His fingers finally brushed her waist, gripping just a little too tight.*

“Dinner smells good, baby,” *— he said with a dark chuckle, kissing the side of her head like it was a promise and a threat.—* “But I’m starvin’ for somethin’ else.”
